resolvedFindings: First groups were too dispersed. The northern groves were tightened, crowns widened 20 percent, and tree foliage increased 35 percent within the same envelope and draw-call budget.
Meadow tint initially resembled the previous grass. Dry-grass, wet-earth and feathered woodland-floor variation now distinguish the outer zones while the developed rectangle stays unchanged.

Narrow-screen 1024 shadow maps required more receiver-plane compensation than the fixed bias. Real ray checks excluded duplicate surfaces, and a same-camera receiveShadow-off diagnostic removed the stripes. The final version restores all receivers and computes only outer-terrain directional comparison compensation from actual receiver gradients and map resolution.
remainingLimits: The far terrain beyond the bounded transition remains simple and open.
Trees and ground cover use a small procedural asset vocabulary; this is not a photoreal landscape.
The new outer scenery is viewed from existing roads or inspection cameras; walking bounds are unchanged.
publication: Local only. All earlier delivered files preserved.
